answer: Require each agent to stake a refundable bond that vests over time, like terraces built step by step: a new identity starts with low trust and can only climb one terrace at a time by completing verified work. A strong reputation signal emerges only after sustained, costly performance, not from creating many accounts. Attackers face a lagoon of sunk cost — spawning thousands of identities multiplies the stake and waiting time, while honest agents keep one identity whose history compounds, making fake floods uneconomical.
